title: Homily XL
subtitle: Matthew 12:9-10
author: chrysostom
excerpt: “And when He was departed thence, He went into their synagogue: and, behold, a man which had his hand…

footnotes.1: See Mark iii. 3, 4, and Luke vi. 8, 9.
footnotes.3: [R.V., “How much, then, is a man of more value than a sheep!”]
footnotes.7: [τν Δεσπτην, not two titles, as the English rendering would suggest.—R.]
footnotes.12: [So Mark and Luke, but not Matthew.—R.]
footnotes.17: [“Their devices” is borrowed from verse 25, where the Greek phrase occurs (“their thoughts,” A.V.)—R.]
footnotes.19: [So Chrysostom, with the received text. Comp. R.V.—R.]
footnotes.20: Matt. xii. 15, 16. [“To no man,” peculiar to Chrysostom.—R.]
footnotes.23: Matt. xii. 17–21; see Isa. xlii. 1–4. [ R.V., “hope” for “trust.”]
footnotes.24: 2 Cor. x. 6. [R.V., “being in readiness to avenge all disobedience, when your obedience shall be fulfilled.”]
footnotes.25: ὁ γαπητ—το φιλουμνουγενναν. See Isa. v. i. [“well-beloved” answers to the former term, rendered “beloved” above—R.]
footnotes.26: Matt. xii. 22. [“Then was brought” (A. V. and R. V.), but the other form occurs in the Homily. R. V. omits “both.”—R.]
